DailyGame.title: DailyGame
DailyGame.description: Represents the odds for a specific upcoming game fetched daily from the API.

commenceTime.description: The timestamp when the game is scheduled to start. Must be a Datetime string

bookmakerOdds.description: Array of odds from different bookmakers.

CompletedGame.title: CompletedGame
CompletedGame.description: Represents the final scores of a completed game, fetched to check results.

commenceTime.description: The timestamp when the game started. Must be a Datetime string

homeScore.description: Final score of the home team.

awayScore.description: Final score of the away team.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to accommodate the 'Bettor's Edge' application's data storage needs, focusing on simplicity and security. The primary collections are `daily_games` and `completed_games`, which store data fetched from the external Odds API. Because the application runs on the Firebase Spark plan and cannot use Cloud Functions, all data fetching and saving is done client-side. Therefore the security rules have been simplified for the minimal access required given the constraints. The structure prioritizes ease of data retrieval and updating by directly saving the fetched data into dedicated collections. Since no user-specific data or complex authorization is involved in this particular request (just storage of fetched data), Authorization Independence and complex access models are not applicable here. The application requirements explicitly mentions client-side data fetching and the use of the Spark plan, which limits server-side processing with Cloud Functions. Therefore, the rules below reflect this architecture where the data being written is assumed to be coming from a trusted source or validated client-side before writing.
